thesis: This episode argues that major technology giants like Google, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Netflix, and Spotify are successfully leveraging their platforms to dominate the future of healthcare, biotech, and media distribution. Specifically, it highlights Google's heavy investment in life sciences, Apple's development of health-measuring wearables, and the broader success of these companies in transitioning consumers to paid models and creating new distribution channels.

claims.claim: Google is investing heavily in healthcare and life sciences, with 60% of their investments last year in that sector.
claims.quote: If you look at where Google is investing, they have a venture capital fund called Google Ventures. As I understand, 60% of their investments last year were in health care and life sciences.

claims.claim: Apple is developing wearable devices like AirPods and Apple Watch to measure physical health data, including voice and FDA-approved hard applications.
claims.quote: If you look at what Apple is doing, both with the AirPods and the watch, they're trying to get closer and closer to your physical body such that they can measure things that are going on, including, for example, your voice with the AirPods, and the Apple Watch, even explicitly now, has an FDA-approved hard application.

claims.claim: Microsoft is also positioning itself to capitalize on the future of healthcare and biotech innovation.
claims.quote: Same goes for Microsoft, by the way. So, So there is basically, in my view, a consensus among the smartest minds in technology that the next major waves of innovation are going to be in healthcare and biotech.

claims.claim: Spotify successfully transitioned free music listeners into a paid behavior model, representing a significant majority of the recorded music business.
claims.quote: And I recognize that opportunity because what Spotify had the potential to do was get all of these. free music listeners back into a paid behavior model. And that's exactly what they've done. And now streaming music represents a significant majority of the recorded music business.

claims.claim: Netflix was one of the great successes of the past decade as a new distribution platform in media.
claims.quote: But one pattern that people have pointed to repeatedly is that there's this kind of pendulum that swings between content being king and being king. And what you saw happen in the past decade was Spotify, Apple Music, Netflix, Amazon Prime, those were new distribution platforms that were the great successes of the past decade.
